product: Personal care (activities of daily living) for elderly, chronically ill and disabled, 78.4% of Q2 2026 revenue ($296.0M), paid by state Medicaid programs, managed care organizations, insurers and private pay (2026-08-03 Q2 PR, primary). Hospice 17.0%, home health 4.6%. Demand driven by an aging population avoiding hospitalization or institutionalization.
demand: Volume-led with rate support: Q2 2026 personal care organic revenue +6.8% on higher volumes plus a 9.9% Texas rate increase (late 2025) and 3.9% Illinois increase (Jan 2026); hospice organic +11.1% on average daily census and revenue per patient day (2026-08-03 Q2 PR, primary). Company targets 3-5% same-store growth.
pricing_power: Wage inflation or caregiver shortage without matching state rate increases; loss of rate support (no Illinois increase next year, Texas uncertain); dilution from AccentCare sub-10% EBITDA until synergies land; Medicaid and Medicare reimbursement cuts; fraud, waste and abuse audit scrutiny; integration cost overruns (2026-08-03 Q2 PR, 2026-09-15 Jefferies).
competition: No Chinese substitute; home personal care is local, labor-intensive and non-tradeable (2026-09-14 PR, primary). Closest substitutes are unpaid family caregiving, lower-cost private-duty or gig caregiver marketplaces, and institutional care. Not found: any direct low-cost foreign substitute for this service.
market_strategy: 2026-09-14 CEO Dirk Allison: AccentCare deal expected to add ~$280M annualized personal care revenue, ~19% increase, accretive (PR, primary). 2026-08-03 Allison: we anticipate acting on meaningful synergies and uncovering further growth opportunities throughout the remainder of 2026. 2026-09-15 CFO Poff: close earliest Q1 2027, synergies in 12-18 months.
bull: Q2 2026 revenue +8.0% and adj EPS +16.1% beat the 3-5% same-store target; personal care organic +6.8% on volume plus Texas 9.9% and Illinois 3.9% rate increases; AccentCare adds ~$280M (~19%) annualized revenue (2026-09-14 8-K).
bear: AccentCare PCS runs sub-10% EBITDA, needs 12-18 months to reach normal margin, closes earliest Q1 2027; BofA cut to Hold 140->125 (2026-09-14); no Illinois rate hike next year; consensus 2027 revenue only +4.9%, so deal may be unmodelled.
falsifier: Q3 2026 results around 2026-11-03 showing same-store growth below the 3-5% target, or the AccentCare deal failing to close by 2027-06-30.
web_what_changed_30_90d: 2026-09-14 signed definitive deal to buy AccentCare personal care division for ~$275M cash, adding ~$280M annualized revenue (~19%) across 10 states, closes earliest Q1 2027 pending HSR (SEC 8-K, primary). 2026-09-14 BofA cut to Hold 140->125; 2026-09-28 Raymond James reiterated Buy 137. 2026-08-10 COO Dixon out, Bickham interim (PR, primary). 2026-08-03 Q2 revenue +8.0%.
web_true_now_not_modelled: Acquired AccentCare PCS runs sub-10% EBITDA vs Addus PCS normal; CFO says 12-18 months to close gap, deal closes earliest Q1 2027, EMR conversion end-2027/early-2028 (2026-09-15 Jefferies). Consensus 2027 revenue only +4.9%, so the deal may be unmodelled. No Illinois rate hike next year; New Mexico helps 2H26.
web_demand_product: Personal care (activities of daily living) for elderly, chronically ill and disabled, 78.4% of Q2 2026 revenue ($296.0M), paid by state Medicaid programs, managed care organizations, insurers and private pay (2026-08-03 Q2 PR, primary). Hospice 17.0%, home health 4.6%. Demand driven by an aging population avoiding hospitalization or institutionalization.
web_price_volume_mix: Volume-led with rate support: Q2 2026 personal care organic revenue +6.8% on higher volumes plus a 9.9% Texas rate increase (late 2025) and 3.9% Illinois increase (Jan 2026); hospice organic +11.1% on average daily census and revenue per patient day (2026-08-03 Q2 PR, primary). Company targets 3-5% same-store growth.
web_bottleneck: Addus bottleneck is caregiver fill rate, hours served vs authorized: 84-85% consolidated, ~upper 80s in Illinois, targeting upper 80s (2026-09-15 Jefferies, aggregator); labor is not the gating factor. It relieves institutionalization and hospitalization risk for aging patients. Integration, back-office and EMR conversion is the next constraint on the AccentCare deal.
web_who_benefits_next: Managed care organizations and value-based care partners gain a scaled lower-cost home care partner (2026-09-14 PR, primary); states gain cost-effective alternatives to nursing homes; caregivers gain scheduling flexibility; second-order: Homecare Homebase EMR (conversions), Evercore (advisor), and Addus own hospice and home health referral funnel.
web_who_loses: Nursing homes and institutional care providers lose census; rival personal care and home care operators such as Gentiva or BrightSpring face a larger lower-cost competitor; rival acquirers lose a scarce large PCS asset now taken by Addus (2026-09-14 PR, 2026-09-15 Jefferies, aggregator).
web_margin_collapse_risk: Wage inflation or caregiver shortage without matching state rate increases; loss of rate support (no Illinois increase next year, Texas uncertain); dilution from AccentCare sub-10% EBITDA until synergies land; Medicaid and Medicare reimbursement cuts; fraud, waste and abuse audit scrutiny; integration cost overruns (2026-08-03 Q2 PR, 2026-09-15 Jefferies).
web_low_cost_substitute: No Chinese substitute; home personal care is local, labor-intensive and non-tradeable (2026-09-14 PR, primary). Closest substitutes are unpaid family caregiving, lower-cost private-duty or gig caregiver marketplaces, and institutional care. Not found: any direct low-cost foreign substitute for this service.
web_ceo_promised: 2026-09-14 CEO Dirk Allison: AccentCare deal expected to add ~$280M annualized personal care revenue, ~19% increase, accretive (PR, primary). 2026-08-03 Allison: we anticipate acting on meaningful synergies and uncovering further growth opportunities throughout the remainder of 2026. 2026-09-15 CFO Poff: close earliest Q1 2027, synergies in 12-18 months.
web_did_they_deliver: Yes: 2026-08-03 Q2 2026 revenue +8.0% and adjusted EPS +16.1%, above the high end of the 3-5% same-store target (PR, primary); fill rate improved to 84-85% as targeted (2026-09-15); HomeCourt acquisition closed 2026-05-01 as announced; Bickham returned 2026-08-10 as promised.
web_what_would_falsify: Observable: if the AccentCare deal fails to close by 2027-06-30 (HSR or regulatory block), or if quarterly same-store growth falls below the 3-5% target (first test at Q3 results around 2026-11-03), or if consolidated fill rate stalls under 85%, or if AccentCare EBITDA margin stays sub-10% beyond 18 months post-close (after 2028-06-30). Also a break below the $96 lowest analyst target.
